newsitem.title: GERMANY: Gene maize could be grown separately -German union.
newsitem.headline: Gene maize could be grown separately -German union.

text.p: German farm union (DBV) president Constantin Freiherr Heereman said genetically-modified maize, if given approval for cultivation in Europe, could be sown in certain regions only to separate it from traditional maize.
A DBV statement quoted him as saying he could well imagine initial sowings, storage and processing in just a few regions.
"That way we could demonstrate to the public the advantages of biotechnology for farming and the environment and eliminate concern over possible risks from food products derived from it," he said.
Heereman said the market introduction in Europe of genetically-altered soybeans developed by U.S. firm Monsanto Co had been a public relations disaster.
Consumers worried about possible health risks had been confronted with new soybeans already mixed in with conventional beans from the U.S. crop and consequently panicked.

The EU has put off until December an application for maize produced by Swiss chemical firm Ciba-Geigy AG, which has been made resistant to the corn borer pest and some pesticides, partly as a result of a anti-soya protests in recent weeks.
The U.S. wants to market this maize, already grown across the Atlantic, in Europe and local plant breeders want to start selling seeds for 1997 EU spring plantings.
